actions.text: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Environment and Public Works. (Sponsor introductory remarks on measure: CR S2895)

dimensions.assessment: Affects rural and exurban smaller municipalities, communities at high risk from fire, and state drinking water revolving fund administrators.
dimensions.evidence: communities at high risk from fire or wildfire in rural areas

dimensions.assessment: Expands eligibility criteria for existing water infrastructure funding programs to include fire suppression benefits.
dimensions.evidence: enhancement of water system delivery and distribution capacity in a rural area to aid in fire suppression

dimensions.assessment: Modifies regulatory priorities for existing revolving funds without specifying new direct federal appropriations or spending amounts.
dimensions.evidence: modify regulations with respect to drinking water State revolving funds

dimensions.assessment: Directs specific administrative revisions to federal code of federal regulations governing drinking water revolving funds.
dimensions.evidence: revise section 35.3505 of title 40, Code of Federal Regulations

dimensions.assessment: Requires regulatory revisions within two years and immediate implementation of the revised rules upon enactment.
dimensions.evidence: Not later than 2 years after the date of enactment of this Act... beginning on the date of enactment of this Act, the Administrator shall implement

missing_information: Dollar amounts or funding allocations redirected by the regulatory changes are not specified.
importance_detail.rationale: Directs the EPA to revise regulations within two years to incorporate water infrastructure for fire suppression into drinking water State revolving funds for rural and high-risk communities.
